note: Thursday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Wed 29 Jul US close — FOMC DECISION DAY. The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting but the decision read HAWKISH: a 9-3 vote with three regional-president dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) preferring an immediate 25bp hike, a deliberately short statement, and Chair Warsh signaling 'won't hesitate' and that prices (not the labor market) will set policy — with no September commitment. Equities sold off hard: Dow -2.19% to 51,594 (worst day since Apr 2025), S&P 500 -1.52% to 7,316.15, Nasdaq -1.74% to 24,443, Russell 2000 -1.61%; VIX jumped +13% to 20.66. Compounding it, the US-Iran pause BROKE overnight — renewed airstrikes and Houthi Red Sea strikes sent Brent +7.9% to ~$90.7 and WTI +6.6% to ~$84.5, with energy the lone gaining sector. The semis rout extended (SMH -4%; >$1trn wiped since 24 Jul). Metals held up as havens (silver ~$57.5 flat, gold ~$4,029). Sentiment slid deeper into Fear (baked CNN ~37, crypto ~29 — the dashboard fetches Fear&Greed LIVE in-browser with these as fallback). Breadth deteriorated on the two-day risk-off. Flows are LAGGED: the freshest BofA/EPFR Flow Show is still the week to 22 Jul (the new week releases Friday) and now PRE-dates the FOMC selloff — labeled as such. CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run, so the 7 sub-components are INFERRED from the composite and cited internals and labeled as such.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index fell -1.52% to 7,316.15 on Wed 29 Jul (FOMC day) — a second straight heavy down day that leaves it still above a rising 125-DMA but with momentum cooling fast off the 7,428 record; neutral tilting fearful. [Inferred — CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run]

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Net new highs turned negative on the two-day selloff (Nasdaq new lows outran new highs in the reference session) as leadership narrowed — a fearful read. [Inferred from exchange data]

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). NYSE decliners led (~1.4-to-1 in the reference session) across both down days and the Summation Index is falling from its 8 May peak — deteriorating breadth, fearful. [Inferred — mcoscillator/Barchart JS-gated this run]

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand skewed heavily hedged through the FOMC risk-off and the semis rout — a fearful tilt consistent with the mid-30s composite and the VIX spike. [Inferred]

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. VIX jumped +13.45% to 20.66 on Wed 29 Jul, back above the 20 line and above its 50-day average as the hawkish hold and oil spike hit — a fearful shift from Tuesday's contained ~18.2. [VIX 20.66 confirmed via Yahoo/Cboe]

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Stocks fell hard while Treasuries ALSO sold off (10Y rose ~7bp to ~4.64% as the market judged the Fed 'behind' on inflation) — bonds gave no haven bid; money fled to gold and oil instead. A fearful stock-vs-bond mix. [Inferred]

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS stayed historically tight (~280bp area, ~16-18th percentile) even through the equity selloff — credit is the last non-fearful gauge, signaling no funding stress yet. [FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, ~277bp wk to 23 Jul; likely modestly wider on the risk-off]

Still a majority above trend, a constructive longer-term backdrop that is cooling. 52-wk range roughly 42-70

Approximate; clean 29 Jul value not retrievable

metrics.value: Falling — the Summation Index has rolled over from its 8 May peak (+471) and two consecutive broad down days deepened the deterioration; a confirmed dated late-July numeric level was not retrievable from free sources this run (StockCharts $NYMO/$NYSI JS-gated). Direction clearly negative

metrics.label: Cumulative NYSE Advance-Decline line trend
metrics.value: Rolling over — the A-D line held up with the ~67-70% >200-DMA breadth into mid-July but has weakened on the 28-29 Jul risk-off as leadership narrowed and the Nasdaq 100 slipped into correction (~-10% from its June peak) on the chip rout (inferred trend read)

metrics.label: % of 11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA
metrics.value: Estimated ~55-64% (roughly 6-7 of 11 sector ETFs) and falling — Industrials (-3.4% Wed) and Tech (-2.4% Wed) led the drop and semis are in correction; Energy was the lone gainer on the oil spike. A clean dated count was not extractable this run (inferred from the deteriorating index-level breadth)

breadth.note: Longer-term breadth is still a majority-above-trend (~62-66% of S&P members over their 200-DMA) but the two-day FOMC-week selloff clearly rolled the internals over: the shorter 50-DMA gauge slipped back to/below the 50% line, decliners led ~1.4:1, net new highs turned negative and the McClellan Summation is falling. Indices dropped hard from records (S&P 7,428->7,316, Nasdaq 100 into a ~-10% correction) on the hawkish hold, the oil spike and the extending chip rout — narrowing, deteriorating participation. Several sub-metrics (exact 200-/50-DMA close, daily A/D, McClellan level, net new highs) were JS-gated or lagged this run and are labeled approximate. The open question: whether the Thu 30 Jul GDP/PCE prints and AAPL/AMZN earnings stabilize the tape or extend the risk-off.

flows.period: BofA 'Flow Show' / EPFR week ending Wednesday 22 July 2026 (still the freshest verifiable weekly — the week-to-29-Jul report releases Friday 31 Jul and is NOT yet out). flows.narrative: The freshest weekly read (to 22 Jul, pre-FOMC) showed a decisive cross-border rotation OUT of developed markets and cash INTO emerging markets — above all China, which posted its record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever (+$21.3bn) and drove EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul on record (+$29.6bn) on H2-stimulus optimism, while US equities bled -$7.2bn and Europe -$1.6bn (UK -$1.2bn, largest since November). Korea drew +$1.5bn (a record +$16.3bn over four weeks) and Japan extended its inflow streak to a 7th straight week (+$1.5bn). Cash left money-markets (-$33.9bn) to fund equities (+$30.4bn overall), bonds (+$14.9bn), gold (+$2.0bn, largest since April) and crypto (+$0.9bn) — a barbell chasing EM/China upside while hedging FOMC-hike and geopolitical risk. IMPORTANT: this snapshot pre-dates the hawkish hold and the Iran-pause breakdown, so the next Flow Show (to 29 Jul, out Friday) will be the tell on whether the risk-on EM tilt survived the selloff. BofA's July FMS still shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM (below the 4% contrarian Cash-Rule SELL trigger); the next FMS lands mid-August.

This pre-dates the 28-29 Jul selloff; with FMS cash at just 3.6% (contrarian sell), the stretched-bullish positioning is exactly what amplified the hawkish-hold drop.

The 2nd-largest weekly EM-equity inflow on record, China-fuelled — the marquee flow of the week and a bid under the HK-tech core into the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal. A pre-shock reading; watch whether it survives the FOMC risk-off.

China's record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever, on stronger-than-expected Politburo stimulus wording and the biggest MLF liquidity injection in five months — corroborated the HK/China-tech bid (Tencent/Alibaba/Xiaomi) even through the semis rout. Pre-dates the 29 Jul selloff.

A 7th consecutive week of Japan-equity inflows — the persistent DM haven within the rotation, on governance reform and BoJ normalization. (Korea separately +$1.5bn, a record +$16.3bn over four weeks.)
Europe joined the US on the outflow side as money chased EM/China — a pause in the 2026 pro-international tilt within the DM complex, with the UK outflow the largest since November.

A large money-market OUTFLOW — cash redeployed into equities, bonds and gold rather than hoarded. BofA's FMS cash level (3.6% of AUM) still trips the contrarian Cash-Rule sell signal; parked cash yields ~3.5-3.75% — the book's productive dry powder into the post-FOMC shakeout now underway.

Broad bond-fund inflows continued as investors added duration alongside gold — a hedge that pre-dates the post-FOMC yield jump (10Y ~4.64%); HY OAS ~277bp signals no credit stress yet. IG/HY split not separately itemized this run.

The largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April, on the FOMC-hike/geopolitical hedge bid — and validated by spot holding ~$4,029 through the FOMC-day equity selloff. Gold's YTD inflow remains a record; BofA flags elevated net-longs. (Crypto funds +$0.9bn the same week.)
